text: Exclusive feature for subscribers sign it or log in Meta AI, the artificial intelligence tool available on WhatsApp, refuses to create campaign material for President Lula (PT) but complies with similar requests involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), according to tests conducted by Mônica Bergamo’s column. The chatbot blocked a poster with the phrase "Lula 13" and generated another with the name "Flávio 22." When questioned, the tool itself acknowledged the inconsistency and attributed it to an automatic safety filter. Folha correspondents in the United States, Argentina and Germany were able to generate Lula posters, including ones with photos, using accounts without Brazilian area codes. Brazilian numbers, even when used abroad, had their requests blocked. Meta says that, "in compliance with Brazil’s election rules, we have temporarily prohibited the recommendation of candidates or the generation of images of them." According to the company, the AI generated material featuring the senator because it did not recognize prompts using only the name "Flávio," and additional measures were taken. After the statement, however, the chatbot continued creating images with "Vote Flávio," but not with "Vote Lula" or "Vote Luiz Inácio." Lula’s campaign took the case to the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Wednesday (14). On Friday (10), it had already announced that it would take the matter to the court and the ANPD over alleged interference by Meta. The TSE ordered the company to provide technical explanations and preserve records. Meta denies the accusations and says it is committed to equal treatment.
